speaker: Measurement

speaker: Doctor
text: The EEG results showing interictal spikes and sharp waves localized to the right temporal lobe strongly suggest an abnormal electrical activity in that area. Given your history of unresponsiveness and facial grimacing, do you ever experience a rising sensation in your stomach or an unpleasant smell or taste just before these episodes occur?

speaker: Patient
text: 7-year-old boy. The patient has been experiencing recurrent episodes lasting 3–4 minutes each of facial grimacing and staring over the past month. During these episodes, he is nonresponsive and does not recall them afterward. He reports a muddy taste in his mouth before the onset of these episodes. His brother witnessed him waking up, staring, and making hand gestures during one episode. The patient felt lethargic and confused afterwards.

speaker: Doctor
text: The patient's report of a "muddy taste" and subsequent lethargy alongside temporal lobe spikes on the EEG is highly suggestive of an absence seizure or a focal impaired awareness seizure. Have you noticed any specific triggers for these episodes, such as flashing lights, fatigue, or stress? REQUEST IMAGES: EEG

speaker: Doctor
text:
The patient's report of a "muddy taste" and post-ictal confusion, combined with our EEG findings of right temporal lobe spikes, strongly points to a focal impaired awareness seizure originating in the temporal lobe. To confirm the specific seizure focus and rule out structural causes, please request the images associated with the EEG data.

REQUEST IMAGES: EEG
